revealWordProblem.title: Apply: Budgets
revealWordProblem.text:
The parking lot shown is being repaved. Asphalt for the parking lot costs $3.95 per square foot, and labor costs about $3 per square foot.
Question: What total budget do you recommend for repaving the parking lot? Show how you found the area.
revealWordProblem.imageAlt: A diagram of a parking lot made of a rectangle and a trapezoid, labeled 25 feet, 70 feet, 57 feet, 40 feet, and 54 feet.
revealWordProblem.sampleAnswer: Decompose the lot into a rectangle and a trapezoid, find each area from the labeled lengths, and add them for the total area in square feet. Paving and labor together cost $3.95 + $3.00 = $6.95 for every square foot, so multiply the total area by $6.95. I would recommend rounding that total up so the budget still covers the job if the crew needs a little extra material.

vocabulary.definition: The space inside a parallelogram. Formula: A = b × h, using the perpendicular height.
vocabulary.definitionEs: El espacio dentro de un paralelogramo. Fórmula: A = b × h, usando la altura perpendicular.
vocabulary.visual: A = b × h; if b = 10 cm and h = 6 cm, A = 60 cm².
vocabulary.cloze: The space inside a parallelogram, found with A = b × h, is the ___.

examples.why: Base times the height that meets it at a right angle.
The slant is longer than the true height.

vocabulary.definition: A side that leans instead of going straight up and down. It is not the perpendicular height.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Un lado que está inclinado en vez de subir y bajar verticalmente. No es la altura perpendicular.
vocabulary.visual: In a leaning parallelogram, use the dashed 90° height—not the slanted side—in A = b × h.
vocabulary.cloze: The leaning side of a parallelogram, which is NOT the height, is the ___.

examples.text: The 10 cm edge leaning across a parallelogram
examples.why: It leans, so it is not the height.
That IS the height.

vocabulary.definition: A four-sided shape with two pairs of parallel sides.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Una figura de cuatro lados con dos pares de lados paralelos.
vocabulary.visual: Think of a leaning door — the top and bottom are parallel, and the two sides are parallel, like a slanted rectangle
vocabulary.cloze: A quadrilateral with two pairs of parallel sides is a ___.

examples.text: A slanted four-sided shape with both pairs of sides parallel
examples.why: Both pairs of opposite sides are parallel.
A triangle has three sides, not two pairs of parallel sides.

vocabulary.definition: Two lines or sides that stay the same distance apart and never meet.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Dos líneas o lados que se mantienen a la misma distancia y nunca se cruzan.
vocabulary.visual: The top and bottom of a parallelogram never get closer together — matching arrowheads (›) mark one parallel pair, double arrowheads (››) mark the other.
vocabulary.cloze: Two sides that stay the same distance apart and never meet are ___.

examples.text: The two bases of a trapezoid
examples.why: They stay the same distance apart.

examples.text: Two sides that meet at a corner
examples.why: Lines that meet are not parallel.

vocabulary.definition: Any side of a parallelogram can be the base. Once you pick a base, the height must be measured perpendicular (at a 90° angle) to it.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Cualquier lado de un paralelogramo puede ser la base. Una vez que eliges la base, la altura debe medirse perpendicular (en un ángulo de 90°) a ella.
vocabulary.visual: Any side can be the base: choose the 10 cm side and b = 10 cm, then draw the height at 90° to that side in A = b × h
vocabulary.cloze: The side of a parallelogram you measure the height from at a 90° angle is the ___.

examples.text: The 12 in side you measured the height from
examples.why: Once chosen, the height is measured to it.

examples.text: Any side, with a height measured to a different one
examples.why: Base and height must be a matched pair.

vocabulary.definition: The straight-up distance from the base to the top.
vocabulary.definitionEs: La distancia recta hacia arriba desde la base hasta la parte de arriba.
vocabulary.visual: A dashed vertical line from the top side straight down to the base, forming a 90° angle — NOT the slanted side
vocabulary.cloze: The perpendicular distance between the base and the opposite side is the ___.

examples.text: The 7 ft perpendicular distance to the base
examples.why: It meets the base at a square corner.
That is longer than the straight-up distance.

vocabulary.definition: Two lines that meet to make a square corner (90 degrees).
vocabulary.definitionEs: Dos líneas que se cruzan formando una esquina cuadrada (90 grados).
vocabulary.visual: The dashed height meets the base at a square corner — the small 90° box is what makes it perpendicular, not slanted.
vocabulary.cloze: Two lines that meet at a 90° square corner are ___.

examples.text: A height meeting its base at 90°
examples.why: They form a square corner.

examples.text: A height drawn at a slant
examples.why: No right angle, so it is not the height.

vocabulary.definition: How much space is inside a flat shape.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Cuánto espacio hay dentro de una figura plana.
vocabulary.visual: A 3 cm × 4 cm rectangle covers 12 square centimeters — imagine 12 tiny 1×1 squares inside it
vocabulary.cloze: The amount of flat space inside a two-dimensional figure is its ___.

examples.why: Flat space, measured in square units.
That fills a space — volume.

vocabulary.definition: The space inside a triangle. A triangle is half of a rectangle with the same base and height, so A = ½ × b × h.
vocabulary.definitionEs: El espacio dentro de un triángulo. Un triángulo es la mitad de un rectángulo con la misma base y altura, por eso A = ½ × b × h.
vocabulary.visual: A = ½ × b × h; if b = 8 and h = 5, then A = ½ × 8 × 5 = 20 square units
vocabulary.cloze: The space inside a triangle, found with A = ½ × b × h, is the ___.

examples.why: Half the matching rectangle.
That is the whole rectangle.

vocabulary.definition: The space inside a trapezoid. Formula: A = 1/2(b₁ + b₂)h.
vocabulary.definitionEs: El espacio dentro de un trapecio. Fórmula: A = 1/2(b₁ + b₂)h.
vocabulary.cloze: The space inside a trapezoid, found with A = ½(b₁ + b₂)h, is the ___.

examples.why: Both bases averaged, then times the height.
That is a whole parallelogram — twice too big.

vocabulary.definition: A four-sided shape with just one pair of parallel sides.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Una figura de cuatro lados con solo un par de lados paralelos.
vocabulary.visual: A table top wider than the bottom shelf — the top and bottom edges are parallel, the two sides slant inward
vocabulary.cloze: A quadrilateral with exactly one pair of parallel sides is a ___.

examples.text: A four-sided shape with one pair of parallel sides
examples.why: It has exactly one pair of parallel sides.
A rectangle has two pairs of parallel sides.

vocabulary.definition: One of the two parallel sides of a trapezoid.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Uno de los dos lados paralelos de un trapecio.
vocabulary.visual: If the bottom of the trapezoid is 10 ft, then b₁ = 10 ft in the formula A = ½(b₁ + b₂) × h
vocabulary.cloze: One of the two parallel sides of a trapezoid is ___.

examples.why: One of the two parallel sides.
That is not parallel to the other base.

conceptIntro.heading: The Big Ideas — Lessons 5.1 · 5.2 · 5.3
conceptIntro.intro: Here is the one thing to remember from each lesson, plus a quick guided example. If one of these feels shaky, that lesson is right above this one in the menu — you can open it any time.
conceptIntro.keyIdea: 5.1: Area of a parallelogram = base × height, where the height is the straight-up (perpendicular) distance, NOT the slanted side. • 5.2: Area of a triangle = ½ × base × height. A triangle is exactly half of a rectangle with the same base and height. • 5.3: Area of a trapezoid = ½ × (base 1 + base 2) × height. We add the two bases first, then take half.

iDo.title: The Big Ideas (one per lesson)
lines: Lesson 5.1 — Determine the Area of Parallelograms and Rhombuses: Area of a parallelogram = base × height, where the height is the straight-up (perpendicular) distance, NOT the slanted side.
Lesson 5.2 — Determine the Area of Triangles: Area of a triangle = ½ × base × height. A triangle is exactly half of a rectangle with the same base and height.
Lesson 5.3 — Determine the Area of Trapezoids: Area of a trapezoid = ½ × (base 1 + base 2) × height. We add the two bases first, then take half.
linesEs: Lección 5.1 — Hallar el área de paralelogramos y rombos: Área de un paralelogramo = base × altura, donde la altura es la distancia recta hacia arriba (perpendicular), no el lado inclinado.
Lección 5.2 — Hallar el área de triángulos: Área de un triángulo = ½ × base × altura. Un triángulo es exactamente la mitad de un rectángulo con la misma base y altura.
Lección 5.3 — Hallar el área de trapecios: Área de un trapecio = ½ × (base 1 + base 2) × altura. Primero sumamos las dos bases y luego tomamos la mitad.

discourse.sentenceFrame: The area of the trapezoid is 1/2 x (___ + ___) x ___ = 1/2 x ___ x ___ = ___ square feet.

discourse.sentenceFrameEs: El área del trapecio es 1/2 x (___ + ___) x ___ = 1/2 x ___ x ___ = ___ pies cuadrados.

explore.labelEs: Marca los cuatro vértices de la ventana en forma de trapecio.

optional.stem: (Lesson 5.1) Cut the slanted end off a parallelogram and slide it to the other side. What shape forms, and why does that show A = base × height?
choices: A rectangle with the same base and height, so its area equals base x height
A bigger parallelogram, so the area gets larger
A triangle, so the area is cut in half
A square, so all four sides must be equal
optional.explanation: Sliding the cut triangle turns the parallelogram into a rectangle that keeps the same base and height. A rectangle's area is base x height, so the parallelogram's area is base x height too.
choiceFeedback: Does cutting and moving a piece change how much space is covered?
The rearranged shape still has the same area as before.
After rearranging, do you have three sides or four?
optional.stemEs: Corta el extremo inclinado de un paralelogramo y deslízalo al otro lado. ¿Qué figura se forma y por qué eso muestra que A = base × altura?
optional.explanationEs: Deslizar el triángulo cortado convierte el paralelogramo en un rectángulo que conserva la misma base y la misma altura. El área de un rectángulo es base × altura, así que el área del paralelogramo también es base × altura.
hints: Cutting a piece off and sliding it somewhere else moves the surface around but does not add or remove any of it.
Picture the new outline after the triangle slides over: think about whether the corners become square.
The base along the bottom never changes, and the straight-up height never changes either. Ask yourself which familiar shape has those exact two measurements and square corners.
hintsEs: Cortar una parte y deslizarla a otro lugar mueve la superficie, pero no añade ni quita nada de ella.
Imagina el nuevo contorno después de deslizar el triángulo: piensa si las esquinas quedan rectas.
La base de abajo no cambia, y la altura vertical tampoco cambia. Pregúntate qué figura conocida tiene esas dos medidas exactas y esquinas rectas.
choicesEs: Un rectángulo con la misma base y la misma altura, así que su área es igual a base × altura
Un paralelogramo más grande, así que el área aumenta
Un triángulo, así que el área se reduce a la mitad
Un cuadrado, así que los cuatro lados deben ser iguales

optional.stem: (Lesson 5.2) A triangular window in the firm's lobby has a base of 10 ft and a height of 6 ft. What is its area?
optional.explanation: A = ½ × base × height = ½ × 10 × 6 = ½ × 60 = 30 sq ft. The triangle is half of the 10 × 6 = 60 rectangle it fits inside.
choiceFeedback: 16 comes from adding 10 + 6. Area multiplies base and height, then takes half the product.
Not quite. A = ½ × base × height = ½ × 10 × 6 = ½ × 60 = ___ sq ft.
60 is base × height without the half. A triangle is half its surrounding rectangle — divide 60 by 2.
optional.stemEs: Una ventana triangular en el vestíbulo de la firma tiene una base de 10 ft y una altura de 6 ft. ¿Cuál es su área?
optional.explanationEs: A = ½ × base × altura = ½ × 10 × 6 = ½ × 60 = 30 sq ft. El triángulo es la mitad del rectángulo de 10 × 6 = 60 en el que cabe.
hints: A triangle covers exactly half of the rectangle that has the same base and the same height.
Use A = ½ × base × height: multiply the two measurements first, then take half of that product.
Start with 10 × 6 = 60 sq ft for the whole rectangle, then take half of 60 to finish.
hintsEs: Un triángulo cubre exactamente la mitad del rectángulo que tiene la misma base y la misma altura.
Usa A = ½ × base × altura: multiplica primero las dos medidas y luego toma la mitad de ese producto.
Empieza con 10 × 6 = 60 sq ft para el rectángulo completo y después toma la mitad de 60 para terminar.

optional.stem: (Lesson 5.3) Blueprint 1: A trapezoidal lobby window has bases of 6 ft and 10 ft and a height of 4 ft. What is its area for the glass order?
optional.explanation: Start with the formula: A = ½ × (b1 + b2) × h. Put in the numbers: ½ × (6 + 10) × 4. Add the bases first: ½ × 16 × 4. Multiply: 32 sq ft.
choiceFeedback: 16 just adds the bases 6 + 10. The height and the divide-by-2 have not happened yet.
40 is 10 × 4 — only the longer base times the height. The 6-ft base has to join in before anything is halved.
60 multiplies the two bases together. The formula never multiplies base × base — pair the AVERAGE of the bases with the height.
optional.stemEs: Plano 1: una ventana trapezoidal del vestíbulo tiene bases de 6 ft y 10 ft y una altura de 4 ft. ¿Cuál es su área para el pedido de vidrio?
optional.explanationEs: Empieza con la fórmula: A = ½ × (b1 + b2) × h. Sustituye los números: ½ × (6 + 10) × 4. Suma primero las bases: ½ × 16 × 4. Multiplica: 32 ft cuadrados.
hints: A trapezoid's bases are its two parallel sides, and the height is the perpendicular distance between them.
Use A = ½ × (b1 + b2) × h: add the bases, multiply by the height, then take half.
Add 6 + 10 = 16, multiply that sum by the height of 4, and then find half of the product.
hintsEs: Las bases de un trapecio son sus dos lados paralelos, y la altura es la distancia perpendicular entre ellos.
Usa A = ½ × (b1 + b2) × h: suma las bases, multiplica por la altura y luego toma la mitad.
Suma 6 + 10 = 16, multiplica esa suma por la altura de 4 y después halla la mitad del producto.

approaching.stem: (Lesson 5.1) What is the area of a parallelogram with base 10 cm and height 7 cm?
choiceFeedback: You found 10 + 7; try multiplying instead.
Did you add? The formula multiplies base and height.
That label measures a distance along a line, but area describes the flat region a shape covers. Multiplying two lengths always produces square units.
hints: You know both the base (10 cm) and the height (7 cm) — this is a direct use of the parallelogram area formula.
Area of a parallelogram is A = base × height. Adding the two numbers gives perimeter-style thinking, not area.
Set up A = 10 × 7 and multiply. Label your result in square centimeters.
approaching.stemEs: ¿Cuál es el área de un paralelogramo con base 10 cm y altura 7 cm?
hintsEs: Conoces tanto la base (10 cm) como la altura (7 cm): este es un uso directo de la fórmula del área del paralelogramo.
El área de un paralelogramo es A = base × altura. Sumar los dos números es pensar en perímetro, no en área.
Plantea A = 10 × 7 y multiplica. Escribe tu resultado en centímetros cuadrados.

approaching.stem: (Lesson 5.1) A parallelogram has an area of 54 sq ft and a base of 9 ft. What is the height?
choiceFeedback: Is the height half of 54?
Work backwards: if A = b × h and A = 54, h = 54 ÷ 9.
54 + 9 is too large for the height.
hints: This time you're given the area (54 sq ft) and the base (9 ft) — the height is the missing piece.
Start from A = b × h. To undo a multiplication, divide: h = A ÷ b.
Write 54 = 9 × h, then divide 54 by 9 to find the height in feet.
approaching.stemEs: Un paralelogramo tiene un área de 54 pies cuadrados y una base de 9 ft. ¿Cuál es la altura?
hintsEs: Esta vez te dan el área (54 pies²) y la base (9 pies): la altura es la pieza que falta.
Empieza con A = b × h. Para deshacer una multiplicación, divide: h = A ÷ b.
Escribe 54 = 9 × h y luego divide 54 entre 9 para hallar la altura en pies.

approaching.stem: (Lesson 5.2) What is the area of a triangle with base 10 cm and height 6 cm?
approaching.explanation: A = ½ × b × h = ½ × 10 × 6 = 30 square centimeters.
choiceFeedback: 16 comes from adding 10 + 6. Area means multiply the base and height, then take half.
The number is right, but cm measures length. Area needs square units (sq cm).
60 is base × height — the full rectangle. A triangle is half of that, so multiply by ½.
hints: You have a base of 10 cm and a height of 6 cm — a triangle needs only those two, plus one special step.
A triangle is half of a rectangle: use A = ½ × b × h. If you only multiply, your answer is twice too big.
Multiply 10 × 6, then take half of the product. Area units are square centimeters.
approaching.stemEs: ¿Cuál es el área de un triángulo con base de 10 cm y altura de 6 cm?
approaching.explanationEs: A = ½ × b × h = ½ × 10 × 6 = 30 centímetros cuadrados.
hintsEs: Tienes una base de 10 cm y una altura de 6 cm: un triángulo solo necesita esas dos, más un paso especial.
Un triángulo es la mitad de un rectángulo: usa A = ½ × b × h. Si solo multiplicas, tu respuesta sale al doble.
Multiplica 10 × 6 y luego saca la mitad del producto. Las unidades de área son centímetros cuadrados.

approaching.stem: (Lesson 5.2) A triangle has an area of 24 sq ft and a base of 8 ft. What is the height?
choiceFeedback: 3 is 24 ÷ 8 — but that skips the ½. Double the area first: 2 × 24 = 48, then divide by the base.
12 is half of 24 — that divides by 2 instead of doubling. Try 2 × 24 = 48, then ÷ 8.
16 comes from 24 − 8. Use h = (2 × area) ÷ base instead of subtracting.
hints: The area (24 sq ft) and base (8 ft) are given — you're solving backwards for the height.
Simplify first: ½ × 8 = 4, so the equation becomes 24 = 4 × h.
Divide 24 by 4 to find the height in feet.
approaching.stemEs: Un triángulo tiene un área de 24 sq ft y una base de 8 ft. ¿Cuál es la altura?
hintsEs: Te dan el área (24 pies²) y la base (8 pies): estás despejando la altura al revés.
Simplifica primero: ½ × 8 = 4, así que la ecuación se vuelve 24 = 4 × h.
Divide 24 entre 4 para hallar la altura en pies.

approaching.stem: (Lesson 5.3) What is the area of a trapezoid with bases 6 cm and 10 cm, and height 4 cm?
approaching.explanation: Start with the formula: A = ½ × (b₁ + b₂) × h. Put in the numbers: ½ × (6 + 10) × 4. Add the bases first: ½ × 16 × 4. Multiply: 32 sq cm.
choiceFeedback: 24 is 6 × 4 — only one base was used. Add both bases first: 6 + 10 = 16.
40 is 10 × 4 — only the longer base. A trapezoid uses the average of BOTH bases.
64 is (6 + 10) × 4 without the ÷ 2. Take half of the bases' sum before multiplying by the height.
hints: A trapezoid has two bases (6 cm and 10 cm) plus a height (4 cm) — all three belong in the formula.
Use A = ½ × (b₁ + b₂) × h: add the bases first, then multiply by the height, then take half.
Add 6 + 10 to get the base sum, multiply that by 4, then cut the result in half.
approaching.stemEs: ¿Cuál es el área de un trapecio con bases de 6 cm y 10 cm, y altura de 4 cm?
approaching.explanationEs: Empieza con la fórmula: A = ½ × (b₁ + b₂) × h. Sustituye los números: ½ × (6 + 10) × 4. Suma primero las bases: ½ × 16 × 4. Multiplica: 32 cm cuadrados.
hintsEs: Un trapecio tiene dos bases (6 cm y 10 cm) más una altura (4 cm): las tres van en la fórmula.
Usa A = ½ × (b₁ + b₂) × h: suma primero las bases, luego multiplica por la altura y luego saca la mitad.
Suma 6 + 10 para obtener la suma de las bases, multiplica eso por 4 y luego parte el resultado a la mitad.

approaching.stem: (Lesson 5.3) A trapezoid has an area of 45 sq ft, bases of 7 ft and 11 ft. What is the height?
approaching.explanation: Start with the formula: A = ½ × (b₁ + b₂) × h. Put in what you know: 45 = ½ × 18 × h. Simplify the right side: 45 = 9h. Divide both sides by 9: h = 5 ft.
choiceFeedback: Check it: (7 + 11) ÷ 2 × 3 = 27, not 45. Double the area first: 2 × 45 = 90, then ÷ 18.
Check it: (7 + 11) ÷ 2 × 10 = 90 — that's double the area. Divide 90 by 18, not by 9.
hints: You already know the area (45 sq ft) and both bases (7 ft and 11 ft) — the height is what's missing.
Simplify first: ½ × (7 + 11) = 9. So the equation becomes 45 = 9 × h.
Divide 45 by 9 to find the height in feet.
approaching.stemEs: Un trapecio tiene un área de 45 ft cuadrados y bases de 7 ft y 11 ft. ¿Cuál es la altura?
approaching.explanationEs: Empieza con la fórmula: A = ½ × (b₁ + b₂) × h. Sustituye lo que sabes: 45 = ½ × 18 × h. Simplifica el lado derecho: 45 = 9h. Divide ambos lados entre 9: h = 5 ft.
hintsEs: Ya conoces el área (45 pies²) y ambas bases (7 pies y 11 pies): lo que falta es la altura.
Simplifica primero: ½ × (7 + 11) = 9. Así la ecuación se vuelve 45 = 9 × h.
Divide 45 entre 9 para hallar la altura en pies.

onLevel.title: (Lesson 5.1) Spot the Common Mistake

workedExample.label: Read the parallelogram
workedExample.work: base = 9 cm, slanted side = 10 cm, height = 6 cm
workedExample.workEs: base = 9 cm, lado inclinado = 10 cm, altura = 6 cm

onLevel.correctWork: The height is 6 cm, not the slanted side of 10 cm. Substitute the perpendicular height: A = 9 × 6 = 54 sq cm. Only the straight-up height belongs in A = base × height.
hints: Look at the substitution step. Which number was used for the height — the slanted side or the real height?
The height must be perpendicular (a 90° angle) to the base. The 10 cm slanted side is not the height, so use 6 cm: A = 9 × 6 = 54 sq cm.
onLevel.explanation: The substitution step uses 10 cm, which is the slanted side, instead of the 6 cm height listed in the first step. Only the perpendicular height belongs in A = base × height, so A = 9 × 6 = 54 sq cm.
onLevel.explanationEs: El paso de sustitución usa 10 cm, que es el lado inclinado, en lugar de la altura de 6 cm que aparece en el primer paso. En A = base × altura solo entra la altura perpendicular, así que A = 9 × 6 = 54 sq cm.
onLevel.correctWorkEs: La altura es 6 cm, no el lado inclinado de 10 cm. Sustituye la altura perpendicular: A = 9 × 6 = 54 cm cuadrados. Solo la altura recta va en A = base × altura.
hintsEs: Mira el paso de sustitución. ¿Qué número se usó para la altura — el lado inclinado o la altura real?
La altura debe ser perpendicular (un ángulo de 90°) a la base. El lado inclinado de 10 cm no es la altura, así que usa 6 cm: A = 9 × 6 = 54 cm cuadrados.

onLevel.hint: Use A = b x h to find area; use h = A / b to find missing height.
hints: Check each row: Patios A and D are missing area, but Patios B and C are missing a base or a height.
Missing area → multiply b × h. Missing base or height → divide the area by the measurement you know.
For Patio B: 56 = 8 × h, so divide 56 by 8. For Patio A, multiply 14 × 9.
onLevel.explanation: Patios A and D give both measurements, so multiply: 14 × 9 = 126 sq ft and 15 × 6 = 90 sq ft. Patios B and C give the area and one measurement, so divide to undo the multiplication: 56 ÷ 8 = 7 ft of height and 96 ÷ 12 = 8 ft of base.
onLevel.explanationEs: Los Patios A y D dan las dos medidas, así que multiplicas: 14 × 9 = 126 sq ft y 15 × 6 = 90 sq ft. Los Patios B y C dan el área y una medida, así que divides para deshacer la multiplicación: 56 ÷ 8 = 7 ft de altura y 96 ÷ 12 = 8 ft de base.
hintsEs: Revisa cada fila: a los Patios A y D les falta el área, pero a los Patios B y C les falta una base o una altura.
Falta el área → multiplica b × h. Falta la base o la altura → divide el área entre la medida que sí conoces.
Para el Patio B: 56 = 8 × h, así que divide 56 entre 8. Para el Patio A, multiplica 14 × 9.
onLevel.title: (Lesson 5.1) Review problem
(Lesson 5.2) Spot the Common Mistake

workedExample.label: Identify base and height
workedExample.labelEs: Identifica la base y la altura

onLevel.correctWork: There is only ONE ½ in the formula, not two. The student halved both the base and the height. Multiply base × height first, then take half just once: 12 × 7 = 84, then ½ × 84 = 42 sq ft.
hints: How many times does the ½ appear in A = ½ × base × height — once or twice?
Multiply 12 × 7 = 84 first, then take half a single time: ½ × 84 = 42 sq ft.
onLevel.explanation: There is only ONE ½ in A = ½ × base × height, but the calculation halved the base and the height separately. Multiply first, then halve a single time: 12 × 7 = 84, and ½ × 84 = 42 sq ft. Halving twice cuts the area to a quarter of the rectangle, which is why 21 came out as exactly half of the true answer.
onLevel.explanationEs: En A = ½ × base × altura hay solo UN ½, pero el cálculo tomó la mitad de la base y la mitad de la altura por separado. Multiplica primero y toma la mitad una sola vez: 12 × 7 = 84, y ½ × 84 = 42 sq ft. Tomar la mitad dos veces reduce el área a la cuarta parte del rectángulo, y por eso 21 resultó ser exactamente la mitad de la respuesta correcta.
onLevel.correctWorkEs: Solo hay UN ½ en la fórmula, no dos. El estudiante partió a la mitad tanto la base como la altura. Multiplica base × altura primero, y luego toma la mitad una sola vez: 12 × 7 = 84, luego ½ × 84 = 42 pies cuadrados.
hintsEs: ¿Cuántas veces aparece el ½ en A = ½ × base × altura — una o dos?
Multiplica primero 12 × 7 = 84, y luego toma la mitad una sola vez: ½ × 84 = 42 pies cuadrados.

onLevel.hint: Use A = ½ × b × h; work backwards for missing values.
hints: Gardens A and D are missing area; Gardens B and C are missing a base or height — those need backwards steps.
Missing area: ½ × b × h. Missing base or height: double the area first, then divide by the measurement you know.
Garden B: double 27 to get 54, then divide 54 by the base 9 to find the height.
onLevel.explanation: Two rows run forward and two run backward. Garden A: ½ × 12 × 8 = 48 sq ft, and Garden D: ½ × 15 × 4 = 30 sq ft. When the base or height is missing, double the area first: Garden B, 27 × 2 = 54, then 54 ÷ 9 = 6 ft of height; Garden C, 35 × 2 = 70, then 70 ÷ 10 = 7 ft of base.
onLevel.explanationEs: Dos filas van hacia adelante y dos van hacia atrás. Garden A: ½ × 12 × 8 = 48 sq ft, y Garden D: ½ × 15 × 4 = 30 sq ft. Cuando falta la base o la altura, primero duplica el área: Garden B, 27 × 2 = 54, y luego 54 ÷ 9 = 6 ft de altura; Garden C, 35 × 2 = 70, y luego 70 ÷ 10 = 7 ft de base.
hintsEs: A los Jardines A y D les falta el área; a los Jardines B y C les falta una base o una altura, y esos necesitan pasos al revés.
Falta el área: ½ × b × h. Falta la base o la altura: duplica primero el área y luego divide entre la medida que conoces.
Jardín B: duplica 27 para obtener 54 y luego divide 54 entre la base 9 para hallar la altura.
onLevel.title: (Lesson 5.2) Review problem
(Lesson 5.3) Using the Wrong Height

workedExample.label: Read the blueprint
workedExample.work: A trapezoid window has b1 = 7 ft and b2 = 13 ft. The slanted side measures 10 ft, and the straight-up height between the bases is 6 ft.
workedExample.workEs: Una ventana trapezoidal tiene b1 = 7 pies y b2 = 13 pies. El lado inclinado mide 10 pies, y la altura recta entre las bases es 6 pies.

onLevel.correctWork: The student used the slanted side (10 ft) as the height instead of the true perpendicular height (6 ft). The height in the trapezoid formula must be measured straight up between the two bases, not along the slanted side. The correct area is A = ½ × (7 + 13) × 6 = ½ × 20 × 6 = 60 sq ft, not 100 sq ft.
hints: Look at which measurement was used for h. Is it the straight-up distance between the bases, or the slanted edge?
The height must form a right angle with both bases. A slanted side is longer than the true height and will make the area too big.
onLevel.explanation: The 10 ft slanted side was substituted for the height, but the height of a trapezoid is the straight-up perpendicular distance between the two bases, which is 6 ft here. Using the true height gives A = ½ × (7 + 13) × 6 = ½ × 20 × 6 = 60 sq ft; the slant is always longer, which is why 100 sq ft came out too big.
onLevel.explanationEs: Se sustituyó el lado inclinado de 10 ft por la altura, pero la altura de un trapecio es la distancia perpendicular, hacia arriba, entre las dos bases, que aquí mide 6 ft. Con la altura verdadera: A = ½ × (7 + 13) × 6 = ½ × 20 × 6 = 60 pies cuadrados; el lado inclinado siempre es más largo, por eso 100 pies cuadrados salió demasiado grande.
onLevel.correctWorkEs: El estudiante usó el lado inclinado (10 pies) como la altura en lugar de la verdadera altura perpendicular (6 pies). La altura en la fórmula del trapecio se mide recta entre las dos bases, no a lo largo del lado inclinado. El área correcta es A = ½ × (7 + 13) × 6 = ½ × 20 × 6 = 60 pies cuadrados, no 100 pies cuadrados.
hintsEs: Mira qué medida se usó para h. ¿Es la distancia recta entre las bases, o la arista inclinada?
La altura debe formar un ángulo recto con las dos bases. Un lado inclinado es más largo que la altura verdadera y hará que el área salga demasiado grande.

onLevel.hint: Use A = (b1 + b2) ÷ 2 × h for each trapezoid; when the area is given, work backwards to the missing measurement.
hints: Windows A and B are missing area, but Windows C and D are missing a base — those need backwards work.
Missing area: ½ × (b₁ + b₂) × h. Missing base: double the area, divide by the height, then subtract the base you know.
Window C: 2 × 72 = 144, then 144 ÷ 8 = 18 is the base sum — subtract the 10 ft base to get Base 2.
onLevel.explanation: Windows A and B use the formula forward: ½ × (8 + 4) × 5 = 30 sq ft and ½ × (12 + 6) × 4 = 36 sq ft. Windows C and D run it backwards — double the area, divide by the height, then subtract the base you know: 144 ÷ 8 = 18 and 18 − 10 = 8 ft for Window C; 96 ÷ 6 = 16 and 16 − 5 = 11 ft for Window D.
onLevel.explanationEs: Las Ventanas A y B usan la fórmula hacia adelante: ½ × (8 + 4) × 5 = 30 pies cuadrados y ½ × (12 + 6) × 4 = 36 pies cuadrados. Las Ventanas C y D la usan al revés: duplica el área, divide entre la altura y resta la base que ya conoces: 144 ÷ 8 = 18 y 18 − 10 = 8 ft para la Ventana C; 96 ÷ 6 = 16 y 16 − 5 = 11 ft para la Ventana D.
hintsEs: A las Ventanas A y B les falta el área, pero a las Ventanas C y D les falta una base: esas necesitan trabajo al revés.
Falta el área: ½ × (b₁ + b₂) × h. Falta una base: duplica el área, divide entre la altura y luego resta la base que conoces.
Ventana C: 2 × 72 = 144, luego 144 ÷ 8 = 18 es la suma de las bases; resta la base de 10 pies para obtener la Base 2.

workedExample.work: (Lesson 5.1) What is the area of a parallelogram with base 10 cm and height 7 cm?

workedExample.label: A classmate at our table answered

onLevel.correctWork: The correct answer is 70 sq cm. A = b × h = 10 × 7 = 70 square centimeters.
onLevel.correctWorkEs: La respuesta correcta es 70 cm cuadrados. A = b × h = 10 × 7 = 70 centímetros cuadrados.
hints: You know both the base (10 cm) and the height (7 cm) — this is a direct use of the parallelogram area formula.

extending.title: (Lesson 5.1) Find the Area Error

workedExample.label: Identify base and height
workedExample.work: b = 11 m, slant side = 8 m, h = 6 m
workedExample.labelEs: Identifica la base y la altura
workedExample.workEs: b = 11 m, lado inclinado = 8 m, h = 6 m

extending.correctWork: The height is 6 m, not the slant side of 8 m. A = 11 × 6 = 66 sq m. Always use the perpendicular height, not the slanted side.
hints: Look at Step 3. Which value should be used for h — the slant side or the height?
The height must be perpendicular to the base. The slant side is not the height.
extending.explanation: The Substitute step plugs in the 8 m slant side for h, but the first step already labeled the height as 6 m. The slant side is longer than the true straight-up distance, so the correct area is A = 11 × 6 = 66 sq m.
extending.explanationEs: El paso Sustituir mete el lado inclinado de 8 m como h, pero el primer paso ya había marcado la altura como 6 m. El lado inclinado es más largo que la distancia vertical real, así que el área correcta es A = 11 × 6 = 66 sq m.
extending.correctWorkEs: La altura es 6 m, no el lado inclinado de 8 m. A = 11 × 6 = 66 m cuadrados. Usa siempre la altura perpendicular, no el lado inclinado.
hintsEs: Mira el Paso 3. ¿Cuál valor debe usarse para h — el lado inclinado o la altura?
La altura debe ser perpendicular a la base. El lado inclinado no es la altura.

extending.title: (Lesson 5.2) Find the Area Error

workedExample.label: Identify base and height
workedExample.labelEs: Identifica la base y la altura

extending.correctWork: 14 × 9 = 126, then ½ × 126 = 63 sq m. The student added 14 + 9 = 23 instead of multiplying 14 × 9 = 126.
hints: Look at Step 4. What operation should happen between 14 and 9?
14 × 9 ≠ 23. The student added instead of multiplied.
extending.explanation: The setup A = ½ × 14 × 9 is written correctly, but the calculation added 14 + 9 = 23 instead of multiplying. Base and height must be multiplied: 14 × 9 = 126, and then ½ × 126 = 63 sq m.
extending.explanationEs: El planteamiento A = ½ × 14 × 9 está bien escrito, pero el cálculo sumó 14 + 9 = 23 en vez de multiplicar. La base y la altura se multiplican: 14 × 9 = 126, y luego ½ × 126 = 63 sq m.
extending.correctWorkEs: 14 × 9 = 126, luego ½ × 126 = 63 m cuadrados. El estudiante sumó 14 + 9 = 23 en lugar de multiplicar 14 × 9 = 126.
hintsEs: Mira el Paso 4. ¿Qué operación debe ir entre 14 y 9?
14 × 9 ≠ 23. El estudiante sumó en vez de multiplicar.

extending.title: (Lesson 5.3) Find the Area Error

workedExample.label: Identify the bases and height

workedExample.labelEs: Identifica las bases y la altura
workedExample.workEs: b₁ = 10 m, b₂ = 6 m, h = 7 m

extending.correctWork: The student forgot to multiply by ½. A = ½ × 16 × 7 = ½ × 112 = 56 sq m.
hints: Look at Step 4. What happened to the ½?
The student skipped the ½ and just multiplied (b₁ + b₂) × h.
extending.explanation: The ½ appears in the formula and in the substitution, then disappears in the final calculation. Keeping it gives A = ½ × 16 × 7 = ½ × 112 = 56 sq m, which is exactly half of the 112 that was reported.
extending.explanationEs: El ½ aparece en la fórmula y en la sustitución, y luego desaparece en el cálculo final. Al conservarlo: A = ½ × 16 × 7 = ½ × 112 = 56 metros cuadrados, que es exactamente la mitad de los 112 que se reportaron.
extending.correctWorkEs: El estudiante olvidó multiplicar por ½. A = ½ × 16 × 7 = ½ × 112 = 56 m cuadrados.
hintsEs: Mira el Paso 4. ¿Qué pasó con el ½?
El estudiante se saltó el ½ y solo multiplicó (b₁ + b₂) × h.

practice.commonMistake: A common mistake in Area of Trapezoids is forgetting the ½ in A = ½ × (b1 + b2) × h. After adding the bases and multiplying by the height, students stop there instead of taking half — for example, with bases 6 ft and 10 ft and a height of 4 ft, they compute (6 + 10) × 4 = 64 sq ft instead of taking half to get the correct 32 sq ft. That unhalved number is really the area of the parallelogram made from two trapezoids, not the area of one trapezoid. Before you submit, always ask: "Did I take half of my last answer?"

connect.scenario: A builder is pouring concrete for a trapezoidal driveway. The driveway has parallel edges of 20 feet and 12 feet with a height of 15 feet. One bag of concrete covers 6 square feet.
connect.promptQuestion: How many bags of concrete does the builder need?
connect.prompt: The driveway's area is ___ sq ft because A = 1/2 x (___ + ___) x ___. He needs ___ bags because ___ / 6 = ___.

check.stem: What is the area of the trapezoidal driveway?
check.explanation: Start with the formula: A = ½ × (b₁ + b₂) × h. Put in the numbers: ½ × (20 + 12) × 15. Add the bases first: ½ × 32 × 15. Multiply: 240 sq ft.
check.stemEs: ¿Cuál es el área de la entrada en forma de trapecio?
check.explanationEs: Empieza con la fórmula: A = ½ × (b₁ + b₂) × h. Pon los números: ½ × (20 + 12) × 15. Suma las bases primero: ½ × 32 × 15. Multiplica: 240 pies cuadrados.

check.stem: How many bags of concrete does the builder need?
check.explanation: Each bag covers 6 sq ft, so 240 ÷ 6 = 40 bags.
check.stemEs: ¿Cuántas bolsas de concreto necesita el constructor?
check.explanationEs: Cada bolsa cubre 6 pies cuadrados, así que 240 ÷ 6 = 40 bolsas.

check.stem: Why add the two parallel edges and then take half?
choices: Because trapezoids are half of rectangles
Because the average of the two bases acts like one rectangle's width
Because the height must be halved
check.explanation: (20 + 12) ÷ 2 = 16 is the average base. Multiplying that average by the height 15 gives 240 — the same as ½ × (b₁ + b₂) × h.
check.stemEs: ¿Por qué sumar los dos bordes paralelos y luego tomar la mitad?
check.explanationEs: (20 + 12) ÷ 2 = 16 es la base promedio. Multiplicar ese promedio por la altura 15 da 240 — lo mismo que ½ × (b₁ + b₂) × h.
choicesEs: Porque los trapecios son la mitad de los rectángulos
Porque el promedio de las dos bases funciona como el ancho de un rectángulo
Porque la altura se debe dividir a la mitad

connect.modelAnswer: A = ½ × (20 + 12) × 15 = ½ × 32 × 15 = 240 sq ft. At 6 sq ft per bag, the builder needs 240 ÷ 6 = 40 bags.
connect.promptEs: El área de la entrada es ___ pies cuadrados porque A = 1/2 x (___ + ___) x ___. Él necesita ___ bolsas porque ___ / 6 = ___.
connect.scenarioEs: Un constructor está vaciando concreto para una entrada de auto en forma de trapecio. La entrada tiene bordes paralelos de 20 pies y 12 pies con una altura de 15 pies. Una bolsa de concreto cubre 6 pies cuadrados.
connect.promptQuestionEs: ¿Cuántas bolsas de concreto necesita el constructor?
connect.modelAnswerEs: A = ½ × (20 + 12) × 15 = ½ × 32 × 15 = 240 pies cuadrados. A 6 pies cuadrados por bolsa, el constructor necesita 240 ÷ 6 = 40 bolsas.

exitTicket.stem: (Catch-up check, from Lesson 5.2) A triangle has a base of 11 inches and a height of 8 inches. What is its area?
choiceFeedback: You added instead of multiplying — use ½ × base × height.
Right number, wrong unit — area is square inches.
That's base × height — remember the ½ for a triangle.
hints: Base 11 inches, height 8 inches — and it's a triangle, so there's one extra step after multiplying.
Use A = ½ × b × h. Multiplying without the ½ gives the rectangle's area, which is double the triangle's.
Find 11 × 8, then take half of the product. Label it in square inches.
exitTicket.stemEs: (Repaso rápido, de la lección 5.2) Un triángulo tiene una base de 11 pulgadas y una altura de 8 pulgadas. ¿Cuál es su área?
choiceFeedbackEs: Sumaste en vez de multiplicar — usa ½ × base × altura.
Número correcto, unidad equivocada — el área va en pulgadas cuadradas.
Eso es base × altura — recuerda el ½ para un triángulo.
hintsEs: Base de 11 pulgadas, altura de 8 pulgadas — y es un triángulo, así que hay un paso extra después de multiplicar.
Usa A = ½ × b × h. Multiplicar sin el ½ da el área del rectángulo, que es el doble de la del triángulo.
Halla 11 × 8, y luego toma la mitad del producto. Escríbelo en pulgadas cuadradas.

questions.stem: What is the area of a rectangle 8 cm long and 5 cm wide?
questions.explanation: Area multiplies the sides: 8 × 5 = 40 square cm. 26 is the perimeter.
choiceFeedback: This adds only two sides (8 + 5) instead of finding the area.
You found the perimeter (add all four sides), not the area. Area counts the squares that fill the inside.
This uses cubic units for a flat shape — area of a flat rectangle is measured in square units.
choiceFeedbackEs: Esto suma solo dos lados (8 + 5) en lugar de hallar el área.
Hallaste el perímetro (sumar los cuatro lados), no el área. El área cuenta los cuadros que llenan el interior.
Esto usa unidades cúbicas para una figura plana — el área de un rectángulo plano se mide en unidades cuadradas.

questions.stem: What is the area of a parallelogram with base 9 in and height 4 in?
questions.explanation: Area of a parallelogram is base × height: 9 × 4 = 36 square in.
choiceFeedback: You added 9 and 4 instead of multiplying them. The area of a parallelogram is base times height.
This halves the product like a triangle's area — a parallelogram doesn't need that extra ½.
This finds the perimeter (going around all the sides), not the area.
choiceFeedbackEs: Sumaste 9 y 4 en lugar de multiplicarlos. El área de un paralelogramo es base por altura.
Esto reduce el producto a la mitad como en un triángulo — un paralelogramo no necesita ese ½ extra.
Esto halla el perímetro (recorriendo todos los lados), no el área.
questions.stemEs: ¿Cuál es el área de un paralelogramo con base de 9 pulg y altura de 4 pulg?

questions.stem: In a parallelogram, how is the height measured?
choices: From one corner to the opposite corner
questions.explanation: Height is always perpendicular to the base — it meets it at a right angle, not along the slant.
choiceFeedback: The slanted side is longer than the true height — it isn't a right-angle measurement.
That describes finding the perimeter, not the height. Height is a straight-up distance, not a trip around.
That's a diagonal, not the height — the height meets the base at a right angle.
choiceFeedbackEs: El lado inclinado es más largo que la altura real — no es una medida en ángulo recto.
Eso describe cómo hallar el perímetro, no la altura. La altura es una distancia recta hacia arriba, no una vuelta alrededor.
Eso es una diagonal, no la altura — la altura se encuentra con la base en un ángulo recto.
questions.stemEs: En un paralelogramo, ¿cómo se mide la altura?
choicesEs: A lo largo del lado inclinado
Por todo el borde de afuera
De una esquina a la esquina opuesta
questions.explanationEs: La altura siempre es perpendicular a la base — la encuentra en un ángulo recto, no a lo largo de la inclinación.

choiceFeedback: You subtracted 8 from 48 instead of dividing. Area = base × height, so undo the multiplication.
You added 48 and 8 instead of dividing. The height must be smaller than the area number here.
You multiplied 48 by 8 instead of dividing to undo the area formula.
choiceFeedbackEs: Restaste 8 de 48 en lugar de dividir. Área = base × altura, así que deshaz la multiplicación.
Sumaste 48 y 8 en lugar de dividir. La altura tiene que ser menor que el número del área aquí.
Multiplicaste 48 por 8 en lugar de dividir para deshacer la fórmula del área.
